facts.statement: Cuspicephalus lived during the Late Jurassic period.
facts.quote: fossil_range: Late Jurassic,

facts.statement: The fossil remains of Cuspicephalus were found in Dorset, England.
facts.quote: Cuspicephalus is an extinct genus of monofenestratan pterosaur known from Dorset in England.

facts.statement: The partial skull of Cuspicephalus was discovered in December 2009 by collector Steve Etches in Kimmeridge Bay, Dorset.
facts.quote: In December of 2009, fossil collector Steve Etches discovered the partial skull of a pterosaur in Kimmeridge Bay on the Isle of Purbeck peninsula of Dorset, England.

facts.statement: Cuspicephalus was formally described in a 2013 study by David Martill and Steve Etches.
facts.quote: The specimen was described in a 2013 study by David Martill and Etches, published in Acta Palaeontologica Polonica.

facts.statement: The species is named Cuspicephalus scarfi.
facts.quote: Based upon the specimen, they established the new genus and species Cuspicephalus scarfi.

facts.statement: The genus name Cuspicephalus means "pointed head" in Latin and Greek.
facts.quote: The generic name is derived from cuspis, Latin for "point", after its pointed rostrum, and a Latinised Greek κεφαλή, kephalè, for "head".

facts.statement: The species name scarfi honors cartoonist Gerald Scarfe, whose art featured pointed noses similar to the animal.
facts.quote: The specific name honours artist and cartoonist Gerald Scarfe, whose caricatures usually feature pointed noses reminiscent of Cuspicephalus.

facts.statement: Cuspicephalus was a small pterosaur with a head longer than its body and an elongated tail.
facts.quote: As a wukongopterid pterosaur, Cuspicephalus would have been a relatively small flying animal with a large head, longer than its torso, and an elongated tail.

facts.statement: Based on a skull 32.6 cm long, Cuspicephalus had an estimated wingspan of 1.2 to 1.75 meters, which is large for a Jurassic pterosaur.
facts.quote: Based on the size of the known skull, 32.6 cm long, it is estimated to have a wingspan of around 1.2 m or 1.75 m, large for a Jurassic pterosaur and significantly larger than its immediate relatives in Wukongopteridae.

facts.statement: Cuspicephalus is distinguished by an extremely slender, triangular skull with a long pointed snout.
facts.quote: It is most readily distinguished from other pterosaurs by the elongate shape of its skull. It is triangular, extremely slender, and has a long pointed rostrum.

facts.statement: Cuspicephalus likely had around thirty pairs of teeth along a straight jaw section.
facts.quote: Around thirty pairs of teeth are thought to have been present overall, and the tooth bearing section of the jaw is entirely straight.

facts.statement: Cuspicephalus had a crest on top of its skull that rose to a height of 1 cm and flattened out.
facts.quote: As with many pterosaurs, a crest is present atop the skull. It begins after the twelve tooth, around a third of the skull's length from the jaw tip, and rises gradually before reaching a height of 1 cm and leveling off to a flat shape broadly parallel with the roof of the skull.

facts.statement: The eye socket of Cuspicephalus had a trapezoid shape with a straight, vertical front edge.
facts.quote: The orbit has a somewhat trapezoid shape. Its front edge is straight and vertical, oriented at a right angle with the straight and horizontal top edge.

facts.statement: The angle between the jaw and the back of the skull in Cuspicephalus was 140 degrees.
facts.quote: The angle between the jawline and the back of the skull is 140°, similar to other wukongopterids and Germanodactylus but unlike most pterodactyloids, which possess larger cranial angles.

facts.statement: The genus Cuspicephalus was named by Martill and Etches in 2011.
facts.quote: genus_authority: Martill & Etches, 2011

facts.statement: The holotype specimen was collected by Steve Etches in December 2009 at Kimmeridge Bay on the Isle of Purbeck in Dorset, England.
facts.quote: Fue colectado en diciembre de 2009 por Steve Etches en Kimmeridge Bay, Isla de Purbeck localizada en la costa de Dorset, Inglaterra.

facts.statement: Cuspicephalus lived during the Early Kimmeridgian of the Late Jurassic, approximately 155.7 to 153 million years ago.
facts.quote: que data de principios del Kimmeridgiense en el Jurásico Superior, hace cerca de 155,7-153 millones de años.

facts.statement: The species is known from the partial holotype skull MJML K1918, which lacks the jaw and teeth.
facts.quote: Cuspicephalus es conocido a partir del holotipo MJML K1918, un cráneo parcial que carece de mandíbula y dentición.

facts.statement: The skull was lightweight and measured 326 millimeters in length.
facts.quote: El cráneo es de constitución ligera y tiene una longitud de 326 milímetros.

facts.statement: The skull was very elongated with a height of only 55 millimeters at the back and a triangular profile.
facts.quote: Es muy alargado, con sólo 55 milímetros de altura en la parte posterior, y tiene un perfil triangular.

facts.statement: Nearly half of the skull's length was occupied by the large nasoantorbital fenestra.
facts.quote: Casi la mitad de esta longitud es ocupada por una abertura craneal grande, la fenestra nasoantorbitalis

facts.statement: The rostral index, calculated by dividing snout length by maximum height, was 5.4, the highest value known for any pterosaur.
facts.quote: El índice rostral sensu Naish & Martill de este hocico, en el que su longitud se divide por su máxima altura, es 5.4, el valor más alto conocido para cualquier pterosaurio.

facts.statement: The snout contained between eleven and twelve teeth, with the upper jaw estimated to have held between twenty-five and thirty teeth.
facts.quote: En el hocico hay entre once y doce dientes, mientras que el total para el maxilar superior se estima entre veinticinco a treinta.

facts.statement: The teeth had a wide base with an oval cross-section.
facts.quote: Poseen una amplia base con una sección transversal oval.

facts.statement: A low longitudinal bony crest extended along the top of the skull behind the snout and over the fenestra.
facts.quote: Sobre la parte superior del cráneo, detrás del hocico y sobre la fenestra se extendía una baja cresta ósea longitudinal.

facts.statement: The crest consisted of vertically oriented fibrous bone that may have supported a higher soft tissue crest.
facts.quote: Consistía en hueso fibroso, dirigido verticalmente, que pudo haber formado la base de una cresta más alta de tejido blando.

facts.statement: The crest began at the position of the twelfth tooth.
facts.quote: La cresta comenzaba sobre la posición del diente duodécimo

facts.statement: The genus name Cuspicephalus is derived from the Latin word for 'cusp' due to the pointed shape of its snout and the Greek word for 'head'.
facts.quote: El nombre del género se deriva del latín cuspi, es decir "punta, cúspide" debido a la forma de punta de su rostro, y el griego cephalus, que significa "cabeza".

facts.statement: The species name honors artist Gerald Scarfe, whose caricatures are characterized by frequently depicting pointed noses.
facts.quote: El nombre de la especie honra al artista y caricaturista Gerald Scarfe por sus caricaturas que se caracterizan por representar frecuentemente narices puntiagudas.

facts.statement: Analysis of twelve assessable features showed that eleven matched traits of the family Wukongopteridae.
facts.quote: Cuspicephalus was found to display nearly every feature; of twelve that could be assessed in the known specimen, eleven matched wukongopterid traits.

facts.statement: A 2021 study placed Cuspicephalus deeply within Wukongopteridae and included it in the subgroup Wukongopterinae alongside Wukongopterus and Darwinopterus.
facts.quote: A 2021 study found it to be deeply nested within Wukongopteridae, and established the subgroup Wukongopterinae to include Wukongopterus, Darwinopterus, and Cuspicephalus to the exclusion of Kunpengopterus.

facts.statement: A 2023 study disputed the classification, suggesting Cuspicephalus belonged to the family Germanodactylidae instead.
facts.quote: Contrastingly, one 2023 study found Cuspicephalus to be a germanodactylid.

facts.statement: A 2024 paper argued that Cuspicephalus was basal within Monofenestrata and that other traditionally classified wukongopterids were actually more closely related to pterodactyloids.
facts.quote: A 2024 paper supporting this idea found Cuspicephalus to be related to Darwinopterus modularis in a basal position within Monofenestrata, with other taxa traditionally considered wukongopterids such as Wukongopterus, Kunpengopterus, Changchengopterus, and other species of Darwinopterus all more closely related to pterodactyloids.

facts.statement: Within the subgroup Wukongopterinae, Cuspicephalus was identified as the closest relative of Darwinopterus.
facts.quote: Within Wukongopterinae, Cuspicephalus was found to be the closest relative of Darwinopterus.

facts.statement: Cuspicephalus was significant as the first wukongopterid discovered outside of China, expanding the group's known geographic and temporal range.
facts.quote: The recognition of a wukongopterid pterosaur from the Kimmeridgian age of the United Kingdom was considered the significant, as it expanded the range of the group geographically and in geologic time.

facts.statement: Cuspicephalus was the first wukongopterid known from outside China, whereas previously known members were five million years older.
facts.quote: Previously known wukongopterids form the Tiaojishan Formation of China were five million years older, with Cuspicephalus being the first known from another part of the world.

facts.statement: The large size of Cuspicephalus expanded the known anatomical diversity of the group, which had previously been known only from very similar, small animals.
facts.quote: Its large size expanded the known anatomical diversity of a group previously only known from animals so similar their distinctiveness had been called into doubt by some studies.

facts.statement: The describers classified Cuspicephalus as a member of the broader group Monofenestrata.
facts.quote: los descriptores situaron a Cuspicephalus como un miembro del grupo más general Monofenestrata

facts.statement: A more exhaustive analysis published in 2015 determined that Cuspicephalus was likely a primitive monofenestrated pterosaur and specifically a member of the group Wukongopteridae.
facts.quote: Un análisis más exhaustivo publicado en 2015 determinó que Cuspicephalus era probablemente un pterosaurio monofenestrado primitivo, y específicamente, un miembro del grupo Wukongopteridae

facts.statement: Cuspicephalus lived during the Kimmeridgian stage, between 154.8 and 152.21 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Kimmeridgian to Kimmeridgian (154.8 to 152.21 million years ago)

facts.statement: The type species of the genus Cuspicephalus is Cuspicephalus scarfi.
facts.quote: Type species: Cuspicephalus scarfi

facts.statement: Cuspicephalus belongs to the parent group Monofenestrata.
facts.quote: Parent group: Monofenestrata

facts.statement: Cuspicephalus is classified within the class Reptilia.
facts.quote: Class: Reptilia

facts.statement: There is only one recorded fossil occurrence of Cuspicephalus in the Paleobiology Database.
facts.quote: Fossil occurrences recorded: 1

facts.statement: The describers did not perform a cladistic analysis to determine the exact phylogenetic position of Cuspicephalus among pterosaurs.
facts.quote: Los descriptores no desarrollaron un análisis cladístico para determinar la situación exacta de Cuspicephalus en la filogenia de los pterosaurios
